extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners seeking expedited examination of U.S. applications via the PCT Patent Prosecution Highway (PCT-PPH)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and best practices for obtaining expedited examination of a U.S. patent application under the two-year PCT Patent Prosecution Highway pilot between the USPTO, JPO and EPO. Covers eligibility relationships, required documents, claim correspondence, disclosure duties, filing procedures, and strategic recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying relationship between U.S. and corresponding PCT application
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. application and the corresponding PCT application must have one of the following relationships: (i) the U.S. application is a national stage entry of the corresponding PCT application; (ii) the U.S. application is a national application which forms the basis for the priority claim in the corresponding PCT application; (iii) the U.S. application is a national stage entry of another PCT application that was filed in any competent Receiving Office and claims priority to the corresponding PCT application; (iv) the U.S. application is a national application claiming priority to or continuing status from the corresponding PCT application; or (v) the U.S. application is a continuing application (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part) of another U.S. application that satisfies at least one of the above requirements (i - iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relationship requirement is foundational to eligibility; continuing applications can qualify only if their parent satisfies one of the listed relationships. The USPTO will require showing which of these relationships applies when requesting participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and petition documents and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must file a Request for Participation in the Patent Prosecution Highway Program and a Petition to Make Special under the Patent Prosecution Highway Program, and pay the petition fee (currently $130).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These filings are required to obtain special status; see electronic filing requirement for submission method. Fee amount stated is the amount at the time of the notice and may change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most recent international work product must be submitted and show patentability indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a copy of the most recent international work product (WO/ISA, WO/IPEA, or IPER) unless it is already of record in the U.S. application, and that work product must indicate that the claim(s) has novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work product is not in English, an English translation is required. If the submitted work product includes any Box VIII observations (clarity/support issues), the applicant must identify and explain why the claim(s) is not subject to the observation; failure to do so makes the U.S. application ineligible. If the international work product is already of record, simply state when it was filed in the U.S. application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the PCT claim(s) indicated as allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless already filed in the U.S. application, the applicant must submit a copy of the claim(s) from the corresponding PCT application that are indicated as having novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability in the most recent international work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PCT claim(s) are not in English, an English translation plus a statement that the translation is accurate is required. If identical claims are already present in the U.S. application and in English, no duplicate submission is necessary—just indicate when the claim(s) were filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: All U.S. application claims must sufficiently correspond to PCT claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in the U.S. application must 'sufficiently correspond' to, or be amended to 'sufficiently correspond' to, one or more of the corresponding PCT application claims indicated as having novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO considers claims to 'sufficiently correspond' where, accounting for translation and claim format differences, the claims are of the same or similar scope, or are narrower in scope. A narrower claim is one that is further limited by an additional feature. Applicants must submit a 'claims correspondence table' indicating how each U.S. claim corresponds to the indicated PCT claim(s). In practice, identical or nearly identical claims are most likely to be accepted; claims that increasingly vary from the patentable claim risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit claims correspondence table
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a claims correspondence table that indicates how all claims in the U.S. application sufficiently correspond to the PCT claim(s) indicated as patentable in the international work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table should map each U.S. claim to one or more indicated PCT claims and explain any differences (e.g., narrowing limitations, translation or format-induced changes). Properly documenting correspondence is essential for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of references cited in international work product
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) listing the documents cited in all international work products (ISR, WO/ISA, WO/IPEA, and IPER) of the corresponding PCT application and must provide copies of those documents (except U.S. patents or U.S. patent application publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such an IDS and copies have already been filed in the U.S. application, the applicant may simply indicate when they were filed. Applicants also retain the continuing duty to disclose to the USPTO all other information known to be material to patentability; participation in PCT-PPH does not relieve this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination of the U.S. application must not have begun
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is ineligible for PCT-PPH if substantive examination of that U.S. application has already begun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the request for PPH is filed before the examiner has commenced substantive examination; if examination starts after defect notification (see non-compliance rules) but before a perfected renewed request, the renewed request will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of request and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request for Participation in the PCT-PPH program and all supporting documents must be submitted to the USPTO electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments or IDSs being filed with the request must be separately indexed. Failure to file electronically as required will render the request non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant requests: cure opportunity and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PCT-PPH request does not meet all requirements, the USPTO will notify the applicant of defects and give one opportunity to perfect the request by filing a renewed request for participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to perfect the request, the USPTO will notify the applicant and the application will await examination in its regular turn. If substantive examination begins after defect notification but before filing the renewed request, the renewed request will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests do not automatically extend to continuing U.S. applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for participation and any special status granted in a parent application will not automatically carry over to a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing applications must separately fulfill all PCT-PPH requirements and file their own requests to obtain special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of patentability indication must be a Trilateral ISA/IPEA work product
rubrics_metrics.description: The favorable indication that at least one claim has novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability must come from one of the Trilateral Offices acting as an international search authority (ISA) or international preliminary examining authority (IPEA), appearing in a WO/ISA, WO/IPEA, or IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications from non-Trilateral ISAs/IPEAs are not sufficient for the Trilateral PCT-PPH pilot; applicants should ensure the work product relied upon originates from a Trilateral Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic recommendations to maximize PCT-PPH effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical strategies include seeking a favorable WO/ISA (routinely available ~18 months from priority) as the basis for PCT-PPH; filing a Chapter II Demand to obtain a WO/IPEA or IPER if WO/ISA is unfavorable; designating a Trilateral Office as ISA/IPEA when possible; filing a continuation (rather than a U.S. national stage entry) to reduce administrative delay when entering the U.S. national phase; and including a set of narrower claims in the PCT to increase the chance of a favorable work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are recommended practices (not formal requirements) intended to increase the likelihood and timeliness of successful PCT-PPH participation. Applicants should weigh these options (e.g., choosing ISA/IPEA, Chapter II demand, continuation vs national stage) based on timing and prosecution strategy.
